chunks: A number of our companions, from Al-Barqi, from his father, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Attar, from a man from our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
He said to me: 'O so-and-so, do you not go forth for your needs? Do you not pass by the greatest Mosque with you in Al-Kufa?' I said, 'Yes.' He said: 'So pray four Rak'at in it.'
Say in them: 'I go forth with the might and power of Allah. I go forth without any might from me nor any power, but with Your might, O Lord, and Your power.'

I ask You for the blessing of this day and the blessing of its people; and I ask You to provide me from Your grace with something permissible and goodly, which You bring to me with Your might and Your power.
And I am humble/submissive in Your well-being.

key_terms.الْمَسْجِدِ الْأَعْظَمِ: The Greatest Mosque (referring to the Great Mosque of Kufa)

ai.seo_question: What is the specific prayer and supplication for seeking livelihood in the Great Mosque of Kufa?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines a specific ritual for seeking sustenance (Rizq) by performing a four-Rak'at prayer in the Great Mosque of Kufa, emphasizing the transition from self-reliance to divine dependence. The prescribed supplication highlights the Shia theological concept of 'Hawl wa Quwwah' (power and might), attributing all capability to Allah while acknowledging human need. This practice underscores the importance of combining physical effort ('going out for needs') with spiritual reliance, a key theme in Shia jurisprudence regarding daily livelihood.
